newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China '97 aluminium sector gloomy - Oriental Metals.
newsitem.headline: China '97 aluminium sector gloomy - Oriental Metals.

text.p: China's aluminium smelters were losing money or suffering badly as electricity prices rose, said Liu Yang, president of China's largest non-ferrous metals trader Oriental Metals (Holdings) Co. Ltd.
"This is a long term problem, because the situation is not very good, because of the electricity cost," said Liu.
"This is a really serious problem, even in 1997," he added, saying the situation would improve but would not match copper's shine.
China would need to import about 100,000 tonnes of aluminium ingots in 1997, and about 800,000 tonnes of alumina, Liu said.
"For the raw material side, China will need 800,000 tonnes of alumina, but it depends on spot market, Liu said.
Imports of alumina were 990,000 tonnes in the first 11 months of 1996, down 1.0 percent from the same period in 1995.
Liu's forecast for aluminium prices in 1997 ranged between $1,550 and $1,750 per tonne on better global demand.
On Friday, aluminium on the London Metal Exchange (LME) held little changed at levels above $1,600 per tonne.
China is expected to produce about 1.74 million tonnes of aluminium in 1996, according to a report in the official China Daily last month.
The country produced a total of 1.5466 million tonnes of aluminium in the first 11 months of 1996, up 2.34 percent from the same period in 1995, the report said.
China's imports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium materials reached 569,018 tonnes in January to November 1996, up by 6.3 percent compared with the year-ago period, customs figures showed.
